title: FadoDB action definition
description: The definition of an action a rule may name (ADR-0045, items 1 and 3): its name, its parameters and what it returns, and what implements it. A definition without a request is the contract of a Go function the host program registers under the same name. A definition with a request is sent by the engine as HTTP, over its connection, with the secrets the host program supplies; ok and result read the reply. A definition holds no code and no secret.

name.description: A namespace and a verb joined by a dot, such as books.post. A name without a dot, and the namespaces table and http, are the engine's. Names match without regard to case.

version.description: The version of the definition, from 1. The database counts it: a redefinition is the next version, and a definition that gives a version gives that one.

description.description: What the action does, for the person or the agent who chooses it.

params.description: The parameters, by name. A rule gives each a formula of its type under args; a json parameter also takes a template, the JSON it becomes with a formula in the place of every string.

returns.description: The values the action returns, by name.

connection.description: The connection the request goes over. The host program names the hosts of each connection and supplies its secrets: a request with a connection goes to those hosts and to no other, and a request without one reads no secret.

name.description: The name by which the host program knows the connection.

secrets.description: The secrets of the connection the request may read with SECRET("name"), and sign with.

request.description: The request the engine sends. Its formulas are pure: they read the parameters and, with SECRET("name"), the secrets of the connection, so every attempt sends the same request. The engine adds Idempotency-Key, the key of the queued action; FadoDB-Event, the id of the event that fired the rule; FadoDB-Attempt; and Content-Type and User-Agent unless the definition gives them.

method.description: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, in any case; POST when absent.

url.description: A formula that gives the address, http or https, as text. URLENCODE makes a value safe for it.

headers.description: Header names to formulas that give their values as text. A header whose formula gives a blank is not sent.

body.description: A template: the JSON to send, with a formula in the place of every string. A body that is one formula giving a text is sent as that text, for a receiver that does not read JSON. Without a body, a POST, a PUT and a PATCH send the call itself (call.schema.json); a GET and a DELETE send none and may not have one.

sign.description: A secret of the connection. The request then carries FadoDB-Signature: t=<seconds since the epoch>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a dot and the body, keyed with the secret>.

ok.description: A condition over the reply, pure, over STATUS, a number, and BODY, the reply as a json value, blank when it is not JSON. A 2xx reply for which it is TRUE is the action run; one for which it is not is a refusal. Without it any 2xx reply is the action run.

result.description: The returned values, each a formula over STATUS and BODY of the type returns declares.

type.description: A scalar type (ADR-0013). int is decimal(0); decimal and money without a scale keep two places.

param.description: A parameter: its type alone, or its type with whether a call must give it and what it is for.

required.description: A call whose argument is blank is refused with required.

returned.description: A returned value: its type alone, or its type with what it is.
